question: Should this PR land the broad Computer Use readiness policy/config/lease surface in core now, or be narrowed to a smaller cache/live-readiness bugfix after the Codex API contract is corrected?
rationale: The root policy treats config/default additions, fail-closed setup, and fallback behavior as compatibility-sensitive, and this PR adds seven knobs plus new fail-closed readiness behavior beyond the narrow stale-cache problem.

options.title: Narrow and prove readiness
options.body: Keep only the supported cache/readiness repair, remove or wire unused knobs, and require a live Computer Use proof before merge.

options.title: Accept the broader surface
options.body: Maintain all new knobs and fail-closed defaults, but require explicit upgrade/default tests and maintainer-visible docs for the new operator behavior.

options.title: Pause for smaller follow-up
options.body: Close or pause this branch if the lease/config scope is not ready for core and ask for a narrower PR focused on the stale-cache failure.

recommendation.title: Narrow and prove readiness
recommendation.body: Keep only the supported cache/readiness repair, remove or wire unused knobs, and require a live Computer Use proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Current main history points to this person on the active Computer Use readiness implementation that would absorb the policy decision.
